claims.text: Integrating containerless levitation, fast differential scanning calorimetry, and in-situ high-energy radiography will enable determination of melting-related thermodynamic properties across a broad range of high-entropy alloys.
The integrated method will determine melting temperatures with ±1–2% accuracy.
The integrated method will determine enthalpies of fusion with ±3–5% accuracy.
The integrated method will determine entropies of fusion with ±3–5% accuracy.
As-cast CoCrCuNi and Al0.5CoCrFeNi samples can provide homogeneous representatives spanning fcc, bcc, and hcp crystal structures.
Containerless processing minimizes heterogeneous nucleation during rapid melting measurements.
Containerless processing minimizes heat loss during rapid melting measurements.
Fast differential scanning calorimetry precisely measures latent heat.
Fast differential scanning calorimetry precisely detects melting transitions.
Real-time neutron radiography can observe melting and liquid-phase morphological evolution in CoCrCuNi-related high-entropy-alloy melts.
High-energy radiography can directly track density changes during HEA melting.
In-situ radiography can directly quantify volume change at melting.
Synchronizing radiography with FDSC directly correlates structural evolution with heat-flow measurements.
Combining containerless processing, FDSC, and imaging yields intrinsic thermodynamic data by reducing artifacts found in conventional DSC.
The integrated method will provide reliable liquid-density measurements.
The integrated method will provide reliable liquid thermal-expansion data.
The measurements will be reproducible across diverse HEA compositions if synchronization is effectively calibrated.
Traditional DSC has container effects, thermal lag, and no direct structural observation, resulting in larger uncertainties in melting-property measurements.
The method is limited to HEAs that are amenable to containerless processing and provide sufficient radiographic contrast.
High-vacuum or inert-atmosphere operation prevents sample contamination.

contradictions.description: The target melting-temperature accuracy is ±1–2%, but the approach is falsified only for deviations greater than 5%. A 2–5% deviation would violate the stated performance target without satisfying the stated falsification criterion.
